inspiration: Sticky target: keep the same target while it is alive, targettable and in range; retarget only when it is lost or out of range (app/core/attacking-state.ts line 26 comment, line 47 branch, lines 62-63 retarget). Keep it for the many-vs-one target choice (rows 2 and 4); change to our leash and hate list.

Conditional finisher targeting: while a status is active, the attacker takes the lowest hit points plus shield among candidates in range (attacking-state.ts lines 34-44). Keep a state that changes target choice (row 13); change the trigger and the visual.

Tie-break by carried item: among candidates at equal distance, prefer those holding a particular item (app/core/pokemon-state.ts line 1137). Keep distance first, then a data tie-break; change the tie-breakers to our own.

Attack timing from speed and frame data: attack duration = 1000 / (0.4 + 0.007 x speed) (attacking-state.ts line 131); the hit lands at a fraction of the animation from per-species frame counts (line 135, types/delays.json); projectile travel time from distance and speed (line 143). Keep the wind-up separate from the cooldown and the hit on the impact frame (rows 6 and 7); change the curve and drop the per-species table.

Command queue then unit update: each step runs queued commands first (simulation.ts line 1314), then each unit updates (blue at line 1332, red at line 1349), with a damage meter sampled just before each unit (lines 1319-1330). Keep deferred hits as commands and a fixed order (row 1, server tick); change to our fixed step.
Pixel-size icon vocabulary: 40 x 40 portraits and 40 x 48 ability icons (samples). Keep one small glyph per ability on a fixed grid for readability at 375 wide (row 14); change the glyph shapes.
Per-species credit records: credits.json holds primary and secondary credits per species with a total. Keep a credit record per asset as data; change the format; never reproduce personal names.

briefs.label: Ranged caster with a visible wind-up
briefs.why: a shot is telegraphed by a short pose before it lands, so the player can read incoming fire
briefs.keep: a delay before the shot equal to a fraction of the attack duration; a travel time from distance
briefs.change: our own projectile, sound and aim line; a different silhouette. Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy. Category-level only (class C)

briefs.label: Lowest-life finisher mode
briefs.why: a status turns a normal attacker into a finisher, which gives a clear mid-fight change
briefs.keep: conditional target override that picks the lowest hit points plus shield in range
briefs.change: our trigger and our visual, not the status name. Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy

briefs.label: Tie-break by carried item
briefs.why: equal-distance targets resolve by something the player can see
briefs.keep: nearest first, then a holder-of-item tie-break
briefs.change: our hate list or class as the tie-break, not an item. Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy

briefs.label: Forty-pixel ability glyph
briefs.why: one small square glyph per ability reads at 375 wide
briefs.keep: a 40 px square icon on a fixed grid, one glyph per ability
briefs.change: our glyph shapes and palette. Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy

briefs.label: Sticky chase target
briefs.why: enemies stop flip-flopping between targets, so a fight reads as one duel
briefs.keep: keep the current target while valid; retarget only when lost
briefs.change: our leash and aggro rules. Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy
